modelterms

modelterms is a lightweight R package providing a unified interface for manipulating stats::terms objects, formulas, fitted models, and character vectors of term labels.

It is designed both as a standalone utility for statistical modeling workflows and as a core infrastructure module for other packages (including midr).

Why modelterms?

In R, model terms serve as the structural blueprint for predictive models—a role of paramount importance in additive models built with stats::lm(), stats::glm(), or GAMs. However, the word “terms” has historically suffered from ambiguity in R. For instance, the terms argument in stats::predict.lm() expects a character vector of term labels, whereas the "terms" object stored inside a fitted model is a formula-like object packed with complex attributes. Despite representing the same structural concepts, they are not directly interchangeable.

Furthermore, while Base R’s stats::terms() and stats::drop.terms() provide powerful formula parsing, working with them programmatically often involves sharp edges:

  1. Inconsistent Coercion: stats::terms() cannot directly coerce a character vector of term labels like c("x1", "x2"), and stats::reformulate(character(0)) throws an error.
  2. Unwanted Reordering & Renaming: Even with keep.order = TRUE, stats::terms() silently rewrites interaction labels based on variable appearance order (e.g., turning c("a", "b:a") into c("a", "a:b")).
  3. Fragile Subsetting: stats::drop.terms() requires numeric indices, loses the response variable by default, and crashes when all predictor terms are dropped.
  4. Ambiguous “Variables”: Base R lacks a unified API to distinguish between term labels (additive components, e.g., "x1:log(x2)"), model variables (transformed expressions in a formula, e.g., "log(x2)"), and underlying raw variables (column names in a data.frame, e.g., "x2").

modelterms resolves all of these issues with a clean, pipe-friendly functional API.

Installation

You can install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ryo-asashi/modelterms")

Core Concepts: Three Levels of Model Components

Consider the formula y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2). modelterms clearly distinguishes three structural levels:

Level Concept Function Output for Example Formula
Term Labels Individual additive components (main effects & interactions) get_labels(x) c("x1", "log(x2)", "I(x1 * x2)", "x1:log(x2)")
Model Variables Distinct predictor expressions (rows of the factors matrix) get_variables(x, raw = FALSE) c("x1", "log(x2)", "I(x1 * x2)")
Raw Variables Underlying column names required in a data.frame get_variables(x, raw = TRUE) c("x1", "x2")

Setting by.term = TRUE in get_variables() returns a named list mapping each term label to its constituent variables:

library(modelterms)

fml_demo <- y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2)
get_variables(fml_demo, raw = TRUE, by.term = TRUE)
#> $x1
#> [1] "x1"
#> 
#> $`log(x2)`
#> [1] "x2"
#> 
#> $`I(x1 * x2)`
#> [1] "x1" "x2"
#> 
#> $`x1:log(x2)`
#> [1] "x1" "x2"

Usage Examples

1. Flexible and Safe Coercion with as_terms()

as_terms() seamlessly converts terms objects, formulas, fitted models (lm, glm, etc.), or character vectors into a valid stats::terms object, while allowing on-the-fly modification of the response variable and intercept.

  • Strict Term Label Vectors (length >= 2): Every element must be a valid single term. Input order and exact interaction notation (such as "b:a") are strictly preserved.
  • Formula Shorthand (length == 1): A single string containing formula operators (e.g., ".^2" or "a * b + c") is expanded as a right-hand side formula expression.
# Preserves exact order and "b:a" notation for term label vectors
t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1"))
get_labels(t1)
#> [1] "b:a" "a"
has_intercept(t1)
#> [1] TRUE

# Expands length-1 formula shorthands (including "." with data)
t2 <- as_terms(".^2", response = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4])
get_labels(t2)
#> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp"
#> [6] "Wind:Temp"

2. Subsetting, Filtering, and Modifying Terms with filter_terms()

filter_terms() is a declarative, crash-safe replacement for stats::drop.terms(), stats::delete.response(), and [.terms. You can subset terms directly by label or index, filter by interaction order or constituent variables, and modify the response or intercept—even if all predictor terms are filtered out.

fml <- log(Ozone) ~ Solar.R + Wind + Temp + Wind:Temp + Solar.R:Wind

# Extract main effects only
fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels()
#> [1] "Solar.R" "Wind"    "Temp"

# Keep terms involving "Wind", but exclude any term involving "Solar.R"
sub_terms <- filter_terms(fml, require = "Wind", remove = "Solar.R")
get_labels(sub_terms)
#> [1] "Wind"      "Wind:Temp"

# Drop specific interactions (order-invariantly) and replace the response variable
filter_terms(fml, drop = "Temp:Wind", response = "Ozone")
#> Ozone ~ 1 + Solar.R + Wind + Temp + Solar.R:Wind
#> attr(,"variables")
#> list(Ozone, Solar.R, Wind, Temp)
#> attr(,"factors")
#>         Solar.R Wind Temp Solar.R:Wind
#> Ozone         0    0    0            0
#> Solar.R       1    0    0            1
#> Wind          0    1    0            1
#> Temp          0    0    1            0
#> attr(,"term.labels")
#> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind"
#> attr(,"order")
#> [1] 1 1 1 2
#> attr(,"intercept")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"response")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,".Environment")
#> <environment: R_GlobalEnv>

# Directly use the filtered terms object to fit a submodel
lm_sub <- lm(sub_terms, data = airquality)
coef(lm_sub)
#>  (Intercept)         Wind    Wind:Temp 
#>  4.187217000 -0.410375120  0.004366689

3. Order-Invariant Term Matching with match_labels()

When users specify interaction terms in plotting or evaluation functions, they may write "Temp:Wind" instead of "Wind:Temp". match_labels() normalizes and matches terms regardless of variable order while safely handling multi-term expressions like "Wind * Temp".

labs <- c("x1", "log(x2)", "x1:log(x2)", "I(1:100):x1")

# Matches reversed interaction notation to the canonical model labels
match_labels(c("log(x2):x1", "x1:I(1:100)", "x1"), labs)
#>    log(x2):x1   x1:I(1:100)            x1 
#>  "x1:log(x2)" "I(1:100):x1"          "x1"

# Safely handles unmatched or invalid expressions ("omit", "pass", or "fail")
match_labels(c("x1", "x1 * x2", "unknown"), labs, nomatch = "pass")
#>      x1 x1 * x2 unknown 
#>    "x1"      NA      NA

Function Reference Summary

  • Coercion & Filtering (returns a terms object): as_terms(), filter_terms()
  • Label Extraction & Matching (returns a character vector): get_labels(), match_labels()
  • Variable & Attribute Extraction: get_variables(), get_response(), get_order()
  • Structural Predicates (returns a scalar logical): has_intercept(), has_response()
